guarantees.claim: cmd_buf_empty is true if and only if cmd_buf_q equals CmdNone.
counting_d becomes 1 when reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe is high; becomes 0 when cmd_update is high and cmd_buf_empty is high; otherwise holds counting_q.
count_d clears to all zeros when reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe or cmd_update is high; increments by 1 when counting_q is true; otherwise holds count_q.
cmd_update is asserted when cmd_q equals CmdManualRun, or when count_q equals SecCmdDelay truncated to WidthCounter bits; otherwise deasserted.
When none of the explicit conditions hold, counting_d retains counting_q, count_d retains count_q, and cmd_update remains 0, ensuring no unintended state changes.
guarantees.cond: combined else of all assign branches

assumptions.claim: reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe is a single-cycle pulse that asserts exactly once per command write; it must not remain high across multiple cycles.
assumptions.cond: when a new command is written via the register interface
assumptions.risk: If qe is a level instead of a pulse, counting_d stays 1 and count_d stays 0 continuously, stalling the delay counter forever and potentially halting all command processing.

assumptions.claim: cmd_q is a stable, glitch-free registered signal that accurately reflects the core's current command and does not spuriously become CmdManualRun.
assumptions.cond: during the combinational evaluation of cmd_update
assumptions.risk: A glitch on cmd_q to CmdManualRun could immediately assert cmd_update, forwarding a delayed command early or executing a manual run out of sequence, breaking the SCA delay protection.

assumptions.claim: The external logic that updates cmd_buf_q correctly stores the written command on a reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe pulse and resets it to CmdNone once the buffered command is consumed and cmd_buf_empty becomes true.
assumptions.cond: when a command is written or consumed
assumptions.risk: If cmd_buf_q is not properly managed, cmd_buf_empty may be incorrect, causing counting to never reset (stuck counting) or reset too early (losing a command).

assumptions.claim: count_q and counting_q are updated on the same active clock edge with count_d and counting_d respectively, forming a single-cycle synchronous loop.
assumptions.cond: while the generate block is active
assumptions.risk: If the registers are not updated synchronously, the finite state machine becomes unreliable and the delay counter may misbehave.

uncertain_points.claim: It is unclear whether reg2hw.cmd.cmd.qe is a pulse or a level signal; the lack of explicit pulse-width documentation may lead to a functional deadlock if it is asserted for multiple cycles.
uncertain_points.cond: when a command register write occurs and remains active
uncertain_points.risk: If qe is held high, the delay counter is continuously reset, causing indefinite stall of all delayed commands and potentially locking the engine.

uncertain_points.claim: The source and setup/hold of cmd_q relative to the clock are not visible; a glitch on cmd_q during evaluation could falsely set cmd_update for a CmdManualRun condition.
uncertain_points.cond: if cmd_q is an asynchronous or combinational signal near the clock edge
uncertain_points.risk: Spurious firing of cmd_update could cause premature command forwarding, violating the SCA delay property or triggering an unexpected manual run.

uncertain_points.claim: No saturation or overflow protection is present on the delay counter; if counting_q is stuck high and cmd_update never fires, count_q could wrap around and cause a spurious cmd_update.
uncertain_points.cond: when count_q reaches the maximum value and wraps to zero
uncertain_points.risk: Erroneous command dispatch could occur long after the intended delay, potentially breaking protocol or security timing.

uncertain_points.claim: The logic that loads and clears cmd_buf_q is outside this chunk; its behavior must be verified to ensure that cmd_buf_empty reliably indicates buffer emptiness at the right time, because it directly gates the reset of counting_d.
uncertain_points.risk: If cmd_buf_q is not cleared when the buffered command is applied, counting may never reset, blocking all subsequent commands.
